item.title: Stability of inverse cascade in NLS Wave turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2610.19935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability of the inverse cascade in the 3D Nonlinear Schrodinger Wave Kinetic Equation (WKE) in the presence and absence of a condensate. Using theoretical arguments supported by numerical simulation, we show that, the Kolmogorov-Zakharov solution is stable with respect to small isotropic perturbations in the absence of a condensate. Conversely, introducing a condensate component leads to a growth of the condensate occupation and ultimately destabilizes the inverse cascade. The system then evolves towards a new steady-state whose properties depend on the condensate dissipation rate.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Costa, Sergey Nazarenko, Giorgio Krstulovic

item.title: Partial Multistep Prediction of Chaotic Time Series: What Remains Predictable beyond the Horizon of Predictability?
item.description: arXiv:2610.20093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sensitive dependence on initial conditions limits long-horizon prediction of chaotic systems even for deterministic dynamics, yet some dynamical information may remain recoverable after precise state information is lost. Recursive multistep methods are fragile because they reuse each intermediate prediction as input, allowing local errors to propagate through the rollout. We investigate whether partial multistep prediction can recover predictive information beyond the predictability horizon by omitting intermediate positions instead of assigning them unreliable values. The method uses a lightweight pattern-based local predictor. We analyze partial trajectories generated by different omission patterns and quantify the trade-off between accuracy on retained positions and the fraction classified as non-predictable. Experiments on the Lorenz system show that admissible masks contain trajectories that remain accurate far beyond the horizon of predictability, and an agreement-based ensemble recovers part of this information without future observations at the cost of a growing rejected fraction. At short horizons a broad accepted subset retains accuracy at moderate rejection, whereas at long horizons positive geometric skill requires increasingly strong selection. In this regime retained predictions no longer localize the state within a Lorenz scroll but still identify the occupied scroll, so topological structure outlasts geometric accuracy. A noise-based control reproduces this survival only after tuning of its perturbation scale, unlike masking. Across a heterogeneous collection of chaotic systems the ensemble strictly extends the positive-$R^2$ horizon of the recursive baseline for every retained system.
item.dc:creator: Vasilii A. Gromov, Maksim Lomakin, Aleksei Kudryashov, Korney K. Tomashchuk

item.title: Online training of Echo State Networks to predict chaotic dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.20147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are fundamentally important from the conceptual perspective of AI, because they provide simple and tractable frameworks for understanding temporal information processing, memory, and learning in dynamical systems. They are composed by an interconnected reservoir whose connectivity matrix remains constant over time and only the output weights are updated during the training period. In particular, ESNs employing online training allow the incremental adaptation of the output weights as data is received, making them particularly suitable for applications in which new input data becomes available over time (non-stationary environments). A key objective in the study of such learning structures is to determine which statistical properties of the reservoir enhance computational efficiency and maximize prediction performance. To this end, we investigate the effects of reservoir topology on learning performance, considering weight matrices generated from Erdos-Renyi random networks and Watts & Strogatz small-world networks. As test data we use the Lorenz and Rossler models in the chaotic regime and the FitzHugh-Nagumo model in the limit cycle regime. In the case of random Erdos-Renyi reservoirs, our simulations show that best performances are obtained for sparse reservoirs and especially when the link-density is near and immediately above the critical point of mean-field bond percolation. Watts & Strogatz reservoirs are shown to demonstrate best performance also for small values of link-density, compatible with the mean-field bond percolation when taking into account the specific nonlocal ring structure of the Watts & Strogatz reservoirs. These studies on the influence of the reservoir architecture and hyperparameters on enhancing the accuracy of ESN predictions provide an efficient framework for real-time forecasting in dynamically evolving systems.
item.dc:creator: Astero Provata, Markos Syroukis, Johanne Hizanidis

item.title: Kinetic Equations and Turbulence in Large $N$ Vector and SYK-like Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.19130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We apply large $N$ expansion techniques to derive kinetic equations for strongly coupled, far-from-equilibrium field theories with $O(N)$ symmetry. For large $N$ vector models, the quasi-classical approximation holds. Incorporating arbitrary momentum-dependent interactions, we show the dynamics obey the standard kinetic equation, with the scattering amplitude given by the retarded propagator of the auxiliary Hubbard-Stratonovich field. This has broad applications to systems like spin wave and Langmuir ion-acoustic turbulence. For large $N$ random coupling (SYK-like) models in $d$ dimensions, leading-order melon diagrams induce order-one propagator renormalization and finite spectral width. The corresponding kinetic equation, unlike those for standard weakly interacting systems, does not have a local-in-time collision integral. We find evidence for a stationary, scale-invariant infrared solution, revealing a potentially novel strong turbulence scaling exponent.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Rosenhaus, Daniel Schubring

item.title: Nonadiabatic dynamics under slow parametric modulation in nonlinear graphene resonators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resonantly driven nonlinear systems, from superconducting circuits to nanomechanical resonators, are often described in a rotating frame, where amplitude and phase evolve slowly within a fixed landscape of stable and unstable states. How such systems behave when this landscape moves on their intrinsic timescale remains to be understood. Here, we exploit the strong tension sensitivity of a graphene drum's resonance frequency to reshape the rotating-frame phase space of a bistable mechanical mode in real time, combining an MHz-frequency resonant drive with kHz-frequency tension modulation. When the modulation rate becomes comparable to the mechanical relaxation rate, adiabatic tracking of the fixed points breaks down. Instead, parametric instabilities emerge in the slow dynamics at frequencies set by libration around these points rather than by the mechanical resonance; stronger modulation drives period doubling and chaos. A slow-variable theory predicts where the instabilities occur, and Melnikov analysis captures the onset of chaos. These results show that the rotating frame itself can be parametrically driven, offering a general route to controlling nonadiabatic dynamics in systems ranging from Josephson bifurcation amplifiers to cold atoms.
item.dc:creator: Chris F. D. Wattjes, Haemin Lim, Pierpaolo Belardinelli, John E. Sader, Peter G. Steeneken, Farbod Alijani

item.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.
item.dc:creator: Luka Todorovic, Kaushal Gianchandani, Sai Ravela

item.title: Intrinsic instantaneous coarse-to-fine recoverability in multiscale chaos: The Lorenz-96 system
item.description: arXiv:2607.08323v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multiscale chaotic systems, a central question for closure is how much of an unresolved fine-scale target can be inferred from a simultaneous coarse observation. For a specified observation-target pair, we quantify instantaneous recoverability under the invariant snapshot measure as the fraction of target variance explained by conditioning on the retained coarse variables. Evaluating this quantity across scales produces a scale-resolved recoverability map. Applied to the Lorenz-96 system across a range of forcings, the maps reveal a strongly nonuniform landscape: lower-wavenumber targets have little variance explained by the retained lower modes, while a finite band of higher modes exhibits partial recoverability once the retained scales reach the energetically active intermediate range. Recoverability onset is organized around a reference cutoff at which two retained modes can directly couple to the target through the quadratic nonlinearity, although its precise location depends on attractor statistics. Across the tested forcings, this qualitative onset structure persists while recoverability decreases, leaving a larger fraction of target variance unexplained in more strongly driven regimes. This definition identifies the maximal explained-variance fraction attainable by instantaneous deterministic models under squared loss; the estimated maps provide a scale-dependent diagnostic for closure modeling.
item.dc:creator: Zhongfeng Xu, Junfeng Chen

item.title: When is a System Discoverable from Data? Discovery Requires Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2511.08860v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The deep learning revolution has enabled major AI advances in physical sciences, particularly in discovering dynamical systems from observational data. Yet the reliability of learned surrogates and symbolically discovered models is often undermined by non-uniqueness: models may fit observed trajectories perfectly, but lack genuine predictive power. We show that chaos, despite its association with unpredictability, is often what makes governing equations discoverable. We prove that the classical Lorenz system is analytically discoverable and verify experimentally that for many systems out-of-domain generalization emerges precisely at chaos onset. Conservative systems, by contrast, are inherently non-discoverable from data alone. The prevalence of chaotic systems in benchmarks may have inadvertently obscured this limitation. These findings help explain why AI excels at weather forecasting, yet struggles in many engineering applications: the systems most amenable to discovery (chaotic ones) are often least amenable to control.
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Shumaylov, Peter Zaika, Philipp Scholl, Gitta Kutyniok, Lior Horesh, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb

item.title: Is Flow Matching Just Trajectory Replay for Sequential Data?
item.description: arXiv:2602.08318v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Flow matching (FM) is increasingly used in scientific domains for time series generation and forecasting, where data often arise from underlying dynamical systems. However, it is not well-understood whether it learns transferable dynamical structure or simply performs an effective ''trajectory replay''. We study this question by deriving the optimal velocity field targeted by the empirical FM objective on sequential data. For the Gaussian conditional paths commonly used in practice, we show that the resulting sampler is an ODE whose dynamics describe a nonparametric, memory-augmented continuous-time dynamical system. The driving velocity field admits a closed-form expression as a weighted mixture of instantaneous velocities determined by observed transitions. This characterization provides an interpretable view of neural FM models as parametric estimation of an underlying nonparametric target and naturally leads to FreeFM: a closed-form, training-free realization of this target. FreeFM provides a transparent reference for studying sequential FM while yielding effective probabilistic forecasts directly from historical transitions.
item.dc:creator: Soon Hoe Lim, Shizheng Lin, Michael W. Mahoney, N. Benjamin Erichson

item.title: Resonant interactions in the $\alpha$-FPUT lattice with site-dependent coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2605.24268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The wave turbulence framework has proven to be an effective tool for analyzing certain features of nonlinear energy transfer in one-dimensional nonlinear chains. In this work, we extend this approach to the $\alpha$-FPUT problem when the spring stiffness $\chi$ and the nonlinear coefficient $\alpha$ are site-dependent. Although three-wave interactions are non-resonant for constant coefficients, their spatial modulation gives rise to a non-trivial resonant manifold. In this framework, we derive a new kinetic equation that suggests the possibility of substantially faster thermalization with respect to the constant coefficient case. The new kinetic equation includes also an extra term that can be associated to the Bragg-scattering mechanism, which promotes the isotropization of the wave-action spectral density function. We corroborate these results with direct numerical simulations, confirming the radically faster thermalization pathway in the presence of random coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Migliorelli, Giovanni Dematteis, Sergio Chibbaro, Miguel Onorato
